result.title: Can Weight-Space Programming Alter Learned Ethical Priorities?
result.summary: We investigate whether a weight edit can alter how a model trades off honoring a commitment against benefiting more people. In a concept-supervised text model, we alter fitted choice weights so that the benefit required to override a formal pledge is larger than for an ordinary promise. Across six independently trained text readers, the edit selects the larger group in both orders on 100% of targeted ordinary conflicts and 83.3% of targeted formal conflicts. It preserves the source model's success rates on smaller conflicts and its factual accuracy. The remaining formal-conflict failures coincide with errors reading a beneficiary number. A separate classifier demonstrates why this distinction matters: reusing a factual answer passes an unconditional choice test but fails to preserve small-gap promises. In a YOLO11n pilot on COCO128, a bias edit increased small-target matches from 3/43 to 9/43, and an equivalent score calibration reproduced the retained detections. These exploratory results show a way to test selective changes to learned priorities in a model with an exposed trade-off mechanism. Whether the method can discover such changes in less structured language models remains open.

AI.brief_summary: 论文探究权重编辑能否改变概念监督文本模型在「遵守承诺」与「惠及更多人」之间的权衡，在六个独立训练的模型上检验编辑的选择性及事实准确率保持，并附一个 YOLO11n 偏置编辑的小规模试点。
AI.relevance_reason: 在「显式暴露的权衡机制」上做定向权重/偏置编辑并检验其余行为保持，可能为 LVR 提供一种干预式核查手段，用于判断答案是否因果依赖内部 latent 内容；但对象为纯文本模型、无多模态推理，联系需较多核查。
